items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: Drummer Ed Shaughnessy, I asked him once if he could define swing.

ctx.x: Who was not called a bopper until after the fact. But the southwestern bands were playing blues and they were playing arrangements of pop tunes that people could get out there on the floor and dance to and they did. When the audiences started sitting down instead of dancing up and standing there was a profound change in the music because sitting down was like listening to Bartok, and standing up was like dancing to Bob Wills.

Well said. Drummer Ed Shaughnessy, I asked him once if he could define swing. And he said he thought he could but, this is a quote, he says, “Youngsters and even oldsters, they mix up the terms to swing and lock it exclusively into jazz music. Now I think bluegrass music swings like hell, without drums, it swings. It’s infectious.” Do you think bluegrass music swings like Ed does?
My problem goes back further than that. When you say “swing” are you referring to a noun or a verb?
